title.narrative: ROAP/CAM02/Cities for all: inclusive, smart and sustainable urban development in Cambodia

description.narrative:
The overall purpose of this programme is to address the needs and challenges of urban citizens and the Government through integration of human security dimensions in promoting sustainable, inclusive and innovative cities in Cambodia. The growth and development of Cambodia’s cities has contributed to the country’s pathway to graduate from Least Developed Country (LDC) status. The urbanization growth rate in Cambodia is approximately four (4) percent over the last decade, 20 percent in 2010 and 24 percent in 2020 respectively.1 It is predicted that about six (6) million of Cambodians will be inhabited in urban areas by 2050.2 However, this urbanization has not necessarily resulted in sustainable and inclusive development. The poor and vulnerable urban communities continue to experience multiple-deprivations, and are unable to benefit from urban opportunities. Similarly, national and sub-national governments lack resources to invest in innovative approaches for the development of smart cities which are responsive to the needs of urban citizens and in line with the rapid advancement of technology to ensure ‘leaving no one behind’. This programme intends to:
a) Assist the Royal Government of Cambodia (hereinafter ‘the RGC’) to develop a National Roadmap on Smart and Sustainable Cities, guiding the pathway to developing a National Policy Framework for Smart and Sustainable Cities by 2025.
b) Advocate and influence for the human dimension of urbanization in line with the RGC’s development policy on urbanization and other urban regulations.
c) Contribute to RGC’s immediate efforts towards post-pandemic economic recovery, covering such aspects as the digital transformation in urban development which accounts for human security. This will be achieved through multi-stakeholder partnerships intervention, including the public private partnership (PPP) and bankable projects on smart cities.
